title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
taper: Recorded by Ken & Judy Lee on a Sony pc-124 cassette deck with Sony dynamic mics on Norelco cassettes. Microphones were set up in the balcony with a 10-20 foot spread.

ai_review.summary: Clear audience tape capturing a fiery late‑1970 show with scorching 'Dancing', stellar 'Easy Wind' and an epic 'Midnight Hour > Lovelight' despite occasional cut‑offs.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience source that, while not pristine, is surprisingly clear and lets the crowd’s energy shine through. The performance shines on the 18‑minute ‘Dancing’ jam, a melodic ‘Easy Wind’, and a powerful ‘Midnight Hour > Lovelight’ finale, with standout moments like the first known rendition of “Friend of the Devil” and rare acoustic numbers. Minor issues include early cuts in some jams and intrusive audience noise, but overall the show is hailed as one of the band’s high‑water marks for 1970.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars and praise the musical performance; recording quality is described as good/clear with only occasional glitches, leading to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced for an audience tape; noted cut‑offs at the ends of ‘Easy Wind’ and ‘Midnight Hour’, plus occasional noisy balcony railing clatter and crowd clapping that can mask instruments.

standout_songs: Friend of the Devil (first known performance)
He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The show bursts open with two intense, funky numbers, then moves into a sprawling ‘Dancing’ jam, followed by an acoustic set that includes the historic ‘Friend of the Devil’. After the acoustic segment the band launches into high‑energy rock (Cosmic Charlie, St. Stephen > Not Fade Away) and closes with the powerful ‘Midnight Hour > Lovelight’, all propelled by a very vocal New York audience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Exceptional melodic and rhythmic playing; his guitar tone is described as perfect throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Creative, peak‑era bass work highlighted (A‑G‑F‑E line reminiscent of Caution jam).
band_member_comments.Bob: Outstanding solo on ‘Easy Wind’; humorous stage banter noted, and his vocal presence praised in the acoustic set.
